headline: Structure-constrained learned search guides RNA, regulatory, and enzyme sequence design
label: Structure Constrained Sequence Design
summary: Preprints and a published enzyme study now pair explicit structural constraints with learned or generative search across RNA, regulatory, and protein design.
synthesis: The common thread is search over sequence or conformational space conditioned on explicit structural or ensemble information. In the design items, mRNAfold co-optimizes in-solution stability, UTR local structure, and codon choice via suboptimal folding, reporting designs about two-fold more stable, while a machine-learning framework yields intrinsic terminators of programmable strength with released tools TerSP and TerFac. The published poly(U) polymerase study combines multi-round GaMD, machine learning, and an ESM3 generative workflow to engineer variants with higher thermostability and catalytic efficiency. Two preprints supply the conformational foundation: OPES multithermal sampling in one replica recovers IDP ensembles matching REST2 and NMR/SAXS for ACTR, and an RNA tetraloop benchmark finds T-REMD most robust for folding free energies. What is new is the joint use of explicit structural constraints with generative or learned search across regulatory, mRNA, and enzyme problems, rather than a shared method established by any single item.
